topics: 👥 Six Hundred Thousand — 'Who knows all secrets' over a multitude of Israel, and Ben Zoma's gratitude
🍽️ The Good Guest and the Bad Guest — Ben Zoma on how to speak of a host's effort
👑 Sages and Kings — four blessings, and Rabbi Yoḥanan's rule to run toward even gentile kings
🤫 Rav Sheshet and the Still Small Voice — a blind sage knows when the king arrives
⚖️ Rabbi Sheila's Trial — 'kingdom on earth is like kingdom in heaven' and the verse that saved him
🏚️ Ruins, Graves, Friends, and Comets — blessings on houses, cemeteries, reunions, oddities, and the sky

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Blessings on Crowds, Kings, Ruins, and Stars
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 58a–58b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf continues the blessings recited on sights. A multitude of Israel earns 'Who knows all secrets', since every mind and face differs; Ben Zoma adds a blessing of gratitude for the labor of others and contrasts the good guest with the bad one. Blessings for Sages and kings lead to two stories about earthly royalty mirroring Heaven: blind Rav Sheshet knowing the king arrives in silence, and Rabbi Sheila escaping a Persian court by praising God's kingdom. The second amud covers houses of Israel inhabited or ruined, Rav Ḥisda's sigh at a fallen house of charity, the blessing over Jewish graves, seeing a friend after thirty days or a year, unusual creatures, and finally the comet and the constellations.

slides.title: 👥 Ben Zoma on the Temple Mount
slides.subtitle: Why a multitude gets 'Who knows all secrets', and what a good guest says

lines.speaker: Rav Hamnuna
lines.text: One who sees multitudes of Israel says: Blessed… חֲכַם הָרָזִים, Who knows all secrets. Over multitudes of gentiles: 'Your mother shall be sore ashamed' (Jeremiah 50:12).

lines.speaker: Tosefta
lines.text: Why? Their minds are unlike each other and their faces are unlike each other — only He Who knows secrets knows every heart.

lines.speaker: Ben Zoma
lines.text: Seeing a crowd from a step on the Temple Mount he added a second blessing: Blessed… Who created all these to serve me.

lines.speaker: Ben Zoma
lines.text: How much did Adam toil before he found bread: plowed, sowed, reaped, sheaved, threshed, winnowed, separated, ground, sifted, kneaded, baked. And I rise and find it all ready. For a garment: sheared, laundered, combed, spun, wove. All nations come to my door.

lines.speaker: Good guest
lines.text: How much trouble the host took for me — so much meat, so much wine, so many loaves — and all of it for me! 'Remember that you magnify his work' (Job 36:24).

lines.speaker: Bad guest
lines.text: What trouble did this host take? I ate one piece of bread, one piece of meat, one cup. Whatever he did, he did for his wife and children. 'Men do therefore fear him' (Job 37:24).

callout.label: Numbers:
callout.text: A multitude is no fewer than six hundred thousand. Ulla: there is no multitude in Babylonia. Yishai, David's father, 'came among men' (I Samuel 17:12) — he went out, came in, and taught with multitudes.

slides.title: 👑 A Table of Blessings on Sights
slides.subtitle: What the Sages instituted for people, houses, graves, and reunions
rows: Sages of Israel / of the nations
Who has shared of His wisdom with those who fear Him / Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood
Same split for kings: 'shared of His glory' vs. 'given of His glory'
A king, Jewish or gentile
Rabbi Yoḥanan: always run to greet him
So that, if one merits, he will distinguish Israel's kings from the nations' kings
Houses of Israel inhabited / in ruins
Who establishes the border of the widow / the true Judge
Gentile houses: Proverbs 15:25 inhabited; Psalms 94:1 in ruins
Graves of Israel
Who formed you in judgment, nourished, sustained, gathered you in judgment, and will raise you in judgment
Mar son of Ravina adds in Rav Naḥman's name: 'Who knows the number of you all… Blessed… Who revives the dead'
A friend after 30 days / after 12 months
Sheheḥeyanu / Who revives the dead
Rav: the dead are forgotten from the heart only after twelve months — 'forgotten as a dead man out of mind… like a lost vessel' (Ps. 31:13)
Spotted, black, red, white, very tall, dwarf, warty people; elephant, monkey, vulture
Who makes creatures different
Amputee, blind, lame, boils: the true Judge — the split is from-birth vs. after-birth
Beautiful creatures and trees
Who has such things in His world

callout.label: A fatal compliment:
callout.text: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua met Rav Ḥanina son of Rav Ika and recited two blessings; he answered that he counted them as six hundred thousand and recited three, adding 'Who knows all secrets'. 'Are you so clever?' They set their eyes on him and he died.

slides.title: 🤫 Rav Sheshet and the Heretic: When Does the King Arrive?
slides.subtitle: A blind sage proves that earthly royalty mirrors the royalty of Heaven

nodes.content: ❓ Everyone goes to greet the king; blind Rav Sheshet goes too. A heretic mocks: 'Whole jugs go to the river — where do broken jugs go?'
🗣️ Rav Sheshet: 'Come and see that I know more than you.' First troop passes with noise — 'the king is coming!' — 'No.' Second troop, louder — 'now!' — 'No.'
🤫 Third troop passes and there is silence. Rav Sheshet: 'Certainly now the king is coming.'

📜 Proof: מַלְכוּתָא דְאַרְעָא כְּעֵין מַלְכוּתָא דִרְקִיעָא. At Horeb the Lord was not in the wind, not in the earthquake, not in the fire — 'and after the fire a still small voice' (I Kings 19:11–13)

columns.label: The blessing
columns.content: When the king came, Rav Sheshet blessed him. The heretic: 'You bless someone you cannot see?'

columns.label: The heretic's end
columns.content: Some say his friends gouged out his eyes; some say Rav Sheshet set his eyes on him and he became a heap of bones

callout.label: The idea:
callout.text: God's revelation came in the silence after the tumult; so the king appears when the noise of the escort stops.

slides.title: ⚖️ Rabbi Sheila Before the Persian Court
slides.subtitle: A flogging, an informer, Elijah's testimony, and a verse turned into a homily

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rabbi Sheila flogs a man who had relations with a gentile woman. The man informs: 'A Jew judges without the king's authority (harmana).' A messenger summons Rabbi Sheila
2️⃣ 'Why did you flog him?' — 'He had relations with a female donkey.' — 'Witnesses?' Elijah appears as a man and testifies
3️⃣ 'Then he deserves death!' — 'Since our exile we have no authority to execute; you do with him as you wish'

4️⃣ While they deliberate he says 'Yours, O Lord, is the greatness…' (I Chronicles 29:11). Asked what he said: 'Blessed is the Merciful One Who gives kingdom on earth like the kingdom of Heaven, and gave you dominion and love of justice.' They hand him a staff: 'Judge!'

5️⃣ Leaving, the informer sneers, 'Does God do miracles for liars?' — 'Scoundrel, are gentiles not called donkeys? "Whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys" (Ezekiel 23:20).' Seeing him go to report this, Rabbi Sheila rules him a rodef — 'if one comes to kill you, kill him first' — and strikes him dead with the staff

6️⃣ Since the verse saved him, he expounds it: greatness = Creation; power = Exodus; glory = sun and moon for Joshua; triumph = fall of Rome; majesty = wars of Arnon; 'all in heaven and earth' = Sisera; kingdom = Amalek; 'exalted' = Gog and Magog; 'head above all' = Rabbi Yoḥanan: even the water-distributor is appointed from Heaven

callout.label: Rabbi Akiva's baraita:
callout.text: Greatness = splitting of the sea; power = plague of the firstborn; glory = giving of the Torah; triumph = Jerusalem; majesty = the Temple.

slides.title: 🏚️ Two Conversations on the Road, and the Sky Above
slides.subtitle: Ulla and Rav Ḥisda at a ruined house; Shmuel and colleagues on comets and constellations

boxes.title: Rav Ḥisda's Sigh
items: At the door of Rav Ḥana bar Ḥanilai's house, Rav Ḥisda sighed. Ulla: Rav says a sigh breaks half the body (Ezek. 21:11); Rabbi Yoḥanan, the whole body (Ezek. 21:12)

'How can I not sigh?' Sixty bakers by day and sixty by night for anyone in need; his hand never left his purse lest a well-born pauper be shamed; four doors to four winds; grain scattered outside in famine years for those ashamed to take by day
Ulla: Rabbi Yoḥanan — since the Temple fell, the houses of the righteous were decreed to fall (Isa. 5:9), and God will restore them as He will restore Mount Zion (Ps. 125:1)
Still unsatisfied: 'It is enough for a servant to be like his master'

boxes.title: Zikin: The Comet
items: The mishna's zikin — Shmuel: a comet. 'The paths of heaven are as clear to me as the paths of Neharde'a, except the comet'
Tradition: a comet never crosses Orion (Kesil); if it did, the world would be destroyed. But we see it cross! Only its glow crosses
Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua: the curtain (vilon) tears and rolls, showing the light of the firmament
Rav Ashi: a star uprooted on one side of Orion; a star on the other side sees it, is startled, and seems to move

boxes.title: Orion, Pleiades, and Ash
items: Job 9:9 puts Orion before Pleiades; Amos 5:8 reverses. Without Orion's heat the world could not stand the cold of Pleiades, and vice versa
If Scorpio's tail did not rest in the River of Fire, no one stung by a scorpion would live — 'Can you bind the chains of Pleiades or loosen the bands of Orion?' (Job 38:31)
Pleiades (Kima): Shmuel — about a hundred (keme'a) stars, clustered or scattered
Ash: Rav Yehuda — Yota, the tail of Aries or the head of Taurus; the tail fits 'Ash with her sons' (Job 38:32)

callout.label: Also on the amud:
callout.text: Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar: when Babylonia was cursed, its neighbors were cursed — 'pools of water' for the bittern (Isa. 14:23); when Samaria was cursed, its neighbors were blessed — 'a place for planting vineyards' (Micah 1:6).

summary.principle: Whatever one sees — a crowd, a king, a ruin, a comet — is an occasion to bless the One Whose kingdom on earth reflects His kingdom in Heaven.

flowSteps.content: 👥 Six hundred thousand of Israel → 'Who knows all secrets'; Ben Zoma adds 'Who created all these to serve me' and teaches the good guest's gratitude
👑 Sages: 'shared' His wisdom (Israel) vs. 'gave' (nations); kings likewise; always run to greet a king

columns.content: 🤫 Rav Sheshet: the king comes in the silence, as God came in the still small voice
⚖️ Rabbi Sheila: 'kingdom on earth like kingdom in Heaven' wins him a judge's staff; I Chr. 29:11 expounded

flowSteps.content: 🏚️ Houses inhabited or ruined; Rav Ḥisda's sigh; graves of Israel; a friend after 30 days or 12 months; 'Who makes creatures different'
🎓 Key Principle: מַלְכוּתָא דְאַרְעָא כְּעֵין מַלְכוּתָא דִרְקִיעָא — earthly kingship mirrors Heaven's, down to the comet that never crosses Orion

quiz.q: Why does one who sees a multitude of Israel recite 'Who knows all secrets'?
o: Because the crowd is gathered for a secret purpose
Because their minds and faces all differ, and only God knows what is in each heart
Because six hundred thousand stood at Sinai
Because Ben Zoma instituted it on the Temple Mount
quiz.e: The Tosefta explains that no two minds or faces are alike, so one blesses the One Who knows the secrets of every heart.

quiz.q: What distinguishes the blessing over Sages of Israel from the blessing over Sages of the nations?
o: Only the first mentions God's name
Israel's Sages: 'Who has shared of His wisdom with those who fear Him'; the nations': 'Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood'
The blessing over gentile Sages is recited only outside Eretz Yisrael
There is no blessing over Sages of the nations
quiz.e: The baraita uses 'shared… with those who fear Him' for Israel's Sages and 'given… to flesh and blood' for the nations' Sages, and the same split for kings.

quiz.q: How did the blind Rav Sheshet know the king had finally arrived?
o: A herald announced him
The heretic told him after the third troop
The third troop passed and there was silence, like the still small voice at Horeb
The noise became loudest at the third troop
quiz.e: Rav Sheshet said royalty on earth is like royalty in Heaven: at Horeb God was not in the wind, earthquake, or fire but in the still small voice, so the king comes in the silence.

quiz.q: Why did the Persian court hand Rabbi Sheila a staff and tell him to judge?
o: Because Elijah testified on his behalf
Because he explained his prayer as blessing God Who grants kingdom on earth like the kingdom of Heaven and gave them dominion and love of justice
Because the man he flogged confessed
Because he agreed to execute the offender
quiz.e: When asked what he had said, Rabbi Sheila explained he had praised God for granting them earthly dominion and love of justice; impressed by his regard for royalty, they gave him a staff and authorized him to judge.

quiz.q: Ulla and Rav Ḥisda pass a ruined house and Rav Ḥisda sighs. What is the point of Ulla's final reply, 'It is enough for a servant to be like his master'?
o: A servant should not build a house larger than his master's
Since God's own house, the Temple, lies in ruins, one need not be distraught that the houses of the righteous are ruined
Rav Ḥisda should not sigh because sighing breaks half the body
Rav Ḥana bar Ḥanilai's house will be rebuilt before the Temple
quiz.e: After citing Rabbi Yoḥanan that the houses of the righteous were decreed to fall with the Temple and will be restored with Mount Zion, Ulla adds that the servant need not fare better than his master, Whose Temple is in ruins.
